page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.large is a dual-vCPU virtual machine belonging to the memory-optimized r7 instance family. Built on KVM hypervisor technology, the server runs on the x86_64 architecture and provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core via hyperthreading. Processing is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, equipped with 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Architectural instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, which assist vectorized and cryptographic tasks.

The instance features 16 GB of memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive operations. There are no GPUs included, and local storage is not bundled, making external network storage mandatory for persistent data and operating system installations. Networking infrastructure provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not allocated complimentarily and must be attached separately.

Benchmark results reveal a divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core tests such as stress-ng and Geekbench register mid-tier performance, with single-core Geekbench scoring 1481.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 27.58 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics, including PassMark CPU (2919.04) and multi-core Geekbench (1730.0), rank in lower percentiles due to the single physical core limit. Memory bandwidth under uncached 256 MB block sizes measures 14.21 GB/sec for reads and 12.7 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET performance reached 1.91 million operations per second, while static web throughput peaked at 3.11 GB/sec.

From a resource allocation perspective, the instance delivers cost efficiency for operations that require significant memory footprints without paying for excess compute cores. Because persistent disk storage must be provisioned externally, total deployment cost reflects detached storage volumes alongside compute capacity. The ecs.r7.large is best suited for memory-bound services such as Redis caching layers, lightweight relational databases, background queue workers, and small-scale ETL pipelines that do not demand extensive parallel multi-core processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.large is a memory-optimized instance designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-core ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, supported by 16 GB of system memory. Vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI are available alongside hardware cryptography acceleration. The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached disks, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In performance evaluations, single-thread computing and text processing place in average tiers, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into lower percentiles due to the two-vCPU hardware ceiling. Offering a qualitative balance of high memory density without the overhead of larger core counts, the ecs.r7.large is well-aligned for in-memory caches, small relational database deployments, lightweight ETL processes, and staging environments.
